 Most recent Most popular 'Hopefully we can fulfill fan's dreams in this competition' published at 22:25 GMT 22:25 GMT 
 FT: Getafe 0-1 Brighton 
 Brighton & Hove Albion 
 Image source, Getty Images Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler speaking to TNT Sports: "These games in the Conference League are different. You have to beat a low block. You have to understand what the opponents are looking for in the game. Therefore, you have to always be patient in these games and I think we did it today. 
 "We didn't play our best game, to be fair. We had a few moments where we were quite lazy with the easy things. We didn't do the simple things on the highest level but in the end we kept a clean sheet, third clean sheet in a row in this tournament and we scored a goal and I think we deserved to win this game."
 On the plan with Pascal Gross after playing 16 games in a row: "At one point we need to manage him as well, but at the moment he just keeps running. He seems to be in a good shape. Today he didn't play the full 90 minutes, also manage the energy from the players like this."
 On Brighton fans getting excited about winning the competition: "They should dream, that's what I always say. We focus on work. We focus on the things we can control. They should dream and hopefully at one point we can fulfil their dream."

 By Michael Emons BBC Sport journalist Brighton maintained their unbeaten record in this season's Conference League with victory in Spain against Getafe. 
 The Seagulls, third in the Premier League, took a 64th-minute lead when Costinha's knockdown was headed home by Malick Yalcouye off the underside of the crossbar.
 Three of the five Conference League winners have come from England - West Ham in 2023, Chelsea in 2025 and Crystal Palace last season - with the Seagulls favourites to lift the trophy in 2026-27.
 They have now won two and drawn one of their three matches in the main phase of the competition and manager Fabian Hurzeler will be pleased with how his side performed in what looked to be one of their toughest fixtures.
 Brighton had twice hit the woodwork when it was goalless with Jaouen Hadjam shooting against the post in the first half and curling an effort that bounced off the top of the bar early in the second.
 Getafe finished seventh in La Liga last season, but are only 13th domestically this time around, with their total of eight league goals the joint lowest in the division.
 Their best chances fell to Ivan Azon, who helped Ipswich Town win promotion to the Premier League last season while on loan from Como, but he was twice denied by goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.
 Brighton did well to blunt the hosts' attacks and did not look like conceding an equaliser as they recorded their 11th clean sheet of the season from 16 matches.
 This was the last of five consecutive away games for Brighton who return to Amex Stadium on Sunday when they host Brentford in the Premier League. 
 The Seagulls' next European action comes on 26 November when they welcome Romanian club Universitatea Craiova to East Sussex.
